steps: Existing audio JSON opens the independent native-backed editor. Changes to volume, independent looping, cue time and restart action survive Chinese/English/Japanese at 390px with visible return/cancel/review/apply controls; review and Cancel leave both the draft and author tree unchanged.
Apply changes only the ordinary unsaved source draft. Ordinary Save updates exactly the reviewed audio JSON; metadata, scene, referenced WAV and other author files remain byte-identical.
The same scene plans, builds and runs through real Godot. The host validates three audio commands (music play, effect play at 0.125s, music restart at 0.5s) and independent audio/actor completion.

Chrome downloads the generated engine project ZIP. Independent verification confirms one deduplicated WAV resource, extraction preserves its exact bytes and settings, and fresh Godot import/run at another path produces identical audio events.

The bundled scene-audio example is copied into a disposable workspace. Existing tracks and cues are edited; this does not test new audio-document creation or resource import.

Generated project ZIP is downloaded by Chrome, independently verified, extracted and run at a new path. It is source-engineering delivery, not a standalone game executable.
